answer: The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money: sparingly and against verified performance, so Sybil inflation is filtered out before it can compound into a decisive advantage. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a dune as the anchor of the cost.
